primitives.name: HAMIR Index Risk Prediction Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The quantitative HAMIR index will be formulated to identify an athlete's propensity for HSI, and more importantly, identify targets for injury mitigation, thereby reducing the global burden of HSI in high-level American football players.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear superposition of morphological, biomechanical, and clinical risk factors; requires independent validation across diverse populations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Applicable when individualized injury risk exceeds a threshold value, triggering targeted intervention protocols.

layer2.telemetry: Post-injury surveillance data, including re-injury rates and recovery timelines

primitives.name: Eccentric Hamstring Strength Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Many player-games are lost due to the lack of a clear understanding of risk factors and the absence of effective meth‐ ods to minimize re-injury.
primitives.assumptions: Strength is measured under controlled laboratory conditions; assumes consistency between lab and field performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Strength drops below a critical threshold, indicating heightened vulnerability to strain.

primitives.name: MRI Muscle-Tendon Volume Assessment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Enrolled participants will complete preseason assessments of eccentric hamstring strength, on-field sprinting biomechanics and muscle–tendon volumes using magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI).
primitives.assumptions: MRI provides accurate segmentation of muscle and tendon compartments; assumes temporal stability of anatomical measurements.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Volume changes indicate pathological remodeling or edema, increasing stiffness and susceptibility to tearing.

layer2.telemetry: Tissue contrast ratios, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics

primitives.name: IMU-Based Sprinting Biomechanics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Enrolled participants will complete preseason assessments of eccentric hamstring strength, on-field sprinting biomechanics and muscle–tendon volumes using magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI).
primitives.assumptions: Inertial measurement units (IMUs) accurately capture joint angles and accelerations; assumes representativeness of sprinting trials.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Biomechanical patterns deviate from optimal ranges, leading to excessive loading on the hamstring MTU.

layer2.telemetry: Joint kinematics, ground reaction forces, stride frequency

The HAMIR Index integrates multiple sovereign primitives into a unified predictive framework. It operates by combining probabilistic estimates of eccentric hamstring strength, MRI-derived muscle-tendon volumes, and sprinting biomechanics within a Bayesian network structure. This allows for dynamic updating of injury risk as new telemetry data streams in, enabling real-time situational awareness. The model's dual nature—prognostic for initial injury and diagnostic for re-injury—exploits the duality between pre-season baseline and post-injury recovery states. Failure occurs when the composite risk score exceeds a predefined threshold, triggering a cascade of corrective actions.
